name: Comfrey — contextual learner of per-asset TACTIC PnL, with a shadow-run rule library as the supervised target generator and a Gârleanu–Pedersen partial-adjustment controller over the resulting asset-level forecast
mechanism:
DATA FLOW. Panel = true UTC daily OHLCV bars from `trader/data.py::aggregate_asset_daily` (open/high/low/close/volume/trade_count per day, `trader/data.py:150-190`; the current `build_daily_panel_from_db` keeps close only, `:190-227`, so a sibling OHLCV builder is the one new data function), PIT 273-asset universe via the 819 POWERED builder (dead coins retained; live names 13→268 by regime, `runs/819_single_asset/POWERED_RESULT.md` coverage table), 2018-10→2026-06 (~2800 days; ~350k live asset-days on 2022-01→2026-06). Per asset i and day t compute (all causal): residual simple return e_{i,t+1} = r_{i,t+1} − β̂_{i,t}·r_{m,t+1} (β̂ trailing 90 d vs equal-weight PIT market), σ̂_{i,t} = Yang–Zhang 30-day daily vol (floored by `VOL_FLOOR`). SHADOW TACTIC LIBRARY, K=8 fixed a priori, each a deterministic causal map from the OHLC panel to a per-asset position p_{i,k,t}∈[−1,1]: k1 trend-30 sign (the frozen 819 rule, `trader/strategy.py:60-77`), k2 trend-10 sign, k3 trend-90 sign, k4 1-day residual reversal −sign(e_{t}), k5 5-day cross-sectional reversal (−rank-z of 5 d residual return), k6 21-day cross-sectional momentum (rank-z), k7 vol-targeted trend-30 (sign × min(1, σ̄/σ̂_YZ)), k8 constant-mix vs hold-shares (control arm only; measured negative, tactics panel corr. 1), plus flat (PnL≡0, never learned, always available). Each tactic runs in shadow on every asset every day at zero cost — they are functions of the panel — and its realised next-day net PnL per unit of the asset's own vol is the TARGET: y_{i,k,t} = [p_{i,k,t}·e_{i,t+1} − c·|p_{i,k,t}−p_{i,k,t−1}|]/σ̂_{i,t}, c = 21 bp (one-sided on turnover, the `trader/` convention `backtest.py:188-190`). Breadth of the supervised problem: ~350k asset-days × 8 tactics ≈ 2.8M target rows OOS, ~0.3M rows in the first training window (2019–2021).

LEARNED OBJECT. One pooled model f(x_{i,t}, k) → E[y_{i,k,t} | x] shared across all 273 assets and all K tactics (tactic id is a categorical input; no per-asset parameters, which is the anti-813 design choice). Features x (~30, standardised cross-sectionally per date): F-range — log σ̂_YZ,30; log(σ̂_YZ,5/σ̂_YZ,30) (vol trend); the intraday roughness ratio q_t = σ̂²_Parkinson,30/σ̂²_close-to-close,30 (=1 under driftless BM, <1 when sub-daily increments trend, >1 when they mean-revert — an OHLC-native variance-ratio statistic estimated with Parkinson's ~5× efficiency, SE ≈ 0.12 on 30 bars vs ≈ 0.26 for a close-based VR of like window); Garman–Klass/Rogers–Satchell variants; vol-of-vol (30 d SD of log daily Parkinson variance); mean |C−O|/(H−L); gap ratio |O_t−C_{t−1}|/(H−L). F-VR (close) — Lo–MacKinlay VR(5), VR(10), VR(30) over 90 d; 30 d lag-1 autocorrelation. F-flow — 20 d dollar-volume rank, dollar-volume shock log(DV_t/DV_20), trade-count shock. F-xs — cross-sectional return dispersion, β̂, idiosyncratic-vol share, market VR(30), market 30 d return, log days-since-listing, rank of 21 d residual return. F-tactic-state — p_{i,k,t}, |Δp_{i,k,t}| (own turnover cost, known), the tactic's trailing 60 d mean PnL on this asset (= the closed-form "strategy momentum" baseline as a feature). Model class: LightGBM regressor, Huber loss (δ=1 in σ-units; crypto tails make L2 targets seed-fragile), ≤300 trees, depth ≤6, lr 0.03, min_leaf 2000, feature_fraction 0.7, 3 seeds (row/feature subsampling — this is where the ≥3-seed goalpost bites); ridge with per-tactic interactions as the linear control; a meta-labeling classifier arm (López de Prado: primary = tactic gives side, secondary = P(y_k>0|x), log-loss, size from calibrated probability) as a pre-registered robustness arm. Justification of GBM over a shared net: 2.8M rows × 30 features is GBM's regime; nets are excluded by the same pre-registered scope choice TASK_915 made (variance/cost, not evidence). Refit: expanding window, quarterly, 21-day purge/embargo between train end and test start; first OOS quarter 2022-Q1 (so BEAR22 is OUT of sample for the learner), OOS through 2026-Q2; predictions clipped to ±0.2 σ-units. Loss is NOT Sharpe-after-cost (810: post-cost objective = turnover artifact) and NOT rank (magnitude in σ-units is needed to compare against cost).

CONTROL LAW AND EXECUTION. Collapse the K predictions to one asset-level forecast of expected residual return per unit position, in σ-units: f_{i,t} = Σ_k μ̂_{i,k,t}·p_{i,k,t} / Σ_k |p_{i,k,t}| (for sign tactics μ̂_k·p_k already carries direction; trend and reversal arms are near-mirror targets, so the pooled model effectively learns one conditional-autocorrelation function g(x) and both arms inherit it). Aim portfolio aim_{i,t} = clip(f_{i,t}/(γ·σ̂_{i,t}), ±w_max=5%) (the `RiskConfig` per-asset cap, `trader/config.py:118`), rescaled to Σ|aim| ≤ 1 and β-neutralised (Σ_i aim_i·β̂_i = 0 via a BTC hedge leg, so the book is market-residual and its bear sign is not the market's). Gârleanu–Pedersen partial adjustment with a no-trade band: x_{i,t} = x_{i,t−1} + θ·(aim_{i,t} − x_{i,t−1}) applied only where |aim − x_{t−1}| > δ; θ ∈ {0.25, 0.5}, δ calibrated on the TRAIN span so expected turnover ≤ 0.06/day, then frozen — never tuned on OOS. Positions enter only where the expected edge over the implied holding time clears cost: |f_{i,t}|·σ̂_i·(1/θ) > 2c. Flat is the default when no asset clears it; the flat share is logged daily. Orders: daily close-to-close rebalance at the UTC bar, taker cost 21 bp assumed (fee16/slip5 as the goalposts require; the operator's real Kraken tier is unrecorded — loops panel pt 1); a maker/limit execution layer is out of scope and would only lower the cost term. Deployable artifact = 8 numpy rules + one GBM file + three controller parameters + a daily log of (asset, chosen tactic, f, position) — a bill of materials, not a policy checkpoint.
math:
CORE IDENTITY (iterated expectations, loops panel): for any causal book w_t, E[gross] = Σ_t E[w_t·E[e_{t+1}|F_t]]. With w_{i,t} = Σ_k a_{i,k,t}p_{i,k,t}, E[y_{i,k,t}|x] = p_{i,k,t}·E[e_{i,t+1}|x, p]/σ̂. The mechanism is therefore a STRUCTURED conditional-mean forecaster and cannot escape the identity; what it changes is the target. For a sign tactic p = sign(S_L), S_L = L-day past return, under joint normality E[sign(S_L)·e_{t+1}] = ρ_L·σ_e·E|S_L|/σ_S = ρ_L σ_e √(2/π) ⇒ m_k ≡ E[y_k] ≈ 0.80·ρ_L in σ-units, where ρ_L = corr(S_L, e_{t+1}). Dao et al. 2016: trend PnL = long-horizon minus short-horizon realised variance ⇒ E[PnL_trend,L] ∝ σ²(VR_L − 1), VR_L − 1 = 2Σ_{j<L}(1−j/L)ρ_j; reversal has the opposite sign. So the learnable quantity is the CONDITIONAL autocorrelation regime g(x) = E[s·e|x], and the target transformation y = s·e turns the multiplicative interaction s(x_trend)·g(x_regime), which a ridge on raw features cannot represent (E_s[s·g] = 0), into a main effect g(x_regime) that a ridge can. That is a representational (bias) gain plus parameter sharing across assets/tactics, not a variance miracle — stated so it is not oversold.

WHAT IS NEEDED TO CLEAR +0.97 NET@21. Book of standardised bets z_i = s_i·e_i/σ̂_i, |w_i| = 1/N over held names, N_eff effective independent bets, σ̄ = mean daily residual vol of held names (≈4.0%; annual 65–85% for crypto residuals). Per-decision net Sharpe: SR_d = √N_eff·(m − c·τ/σ̄), with τ = Σ|Δw| per day and c = 0.0021. Target SR_d = 0.97/√365 = 0.0508 (0.56 bar → 0.0293). Cost term c·τ/σ̄: τ = 0.155 (the 819 book, `trader/backtest.py:455-462`) → 0.0081; τ = 0.06 → 0.00315; τ = 0.03 → 0.0016. Required m: N_eff=10, τ=0.06 → 0.0508/3.16 + 0.00315 = 0.0192; N_eff=20, τ=0.06 → 0.0114 + 0.00315 = 0.0145; N_eff=10, τ=0.155 → 0.0242; for the +0.56 bar at N_eff=10, τ=0.06 → 0.0124. In per-date IC terms (for ±1 forecasts on unit-variance standardised targets m ≈ IC): IC ≈ 0.015–0.024 — the same order as TASK_915 G-A's 0.02–0.03, from a different estimator. In autocorrelation terms: |ρ_L| among SELECTED (asset, day) ≈ m/0.80 ≈ 0.018–0.030; for a flat lag profile ρ_j = ρ (j ≤ 30), corr(S_30, e) ≈ √30·ρ ⇒ ρ ≈ 0.0035–0.0055 ⇒ |VR(30) − 1| ≈ 29ρ ≈ 0.10–0.16. Calibration against the record: the 819 PIT book (gross +0.74 full span, net@21 +0.56 ⇒ cost 0.18 Sharpe = 0.0094 SR_d) implies √N_eff·0.0021·0.152/σ̄ = 0.0094 ⇒ N_eff ≈ 1.4 at σ̄ = 0.04 — a directional crypto trend book is ~one bet — and m ≈ 0.033, ρ_30 ≈ 0.04, VR(30) ≈ 1.2 averaged over 2018–2025; on BULL24/CHOP25 (gross +0.13/+0.22) m ≈ 0.006–0.010, VR(30) ≈ 1.03. The ask is therefore: find from x a sub-population with |VR(30)−1| ≥ 0.10–0.16 and the right sign, when the unconditional 2024–26 average is ≈ 0.03 — dispersion of conditional autocorrelation, not its level. COST DRAG in annualised Sharpe on a residual book: √N_eff·(cτ/σ̄)·√365 = 0.19 at (N_eff 10, τ 0.06) vs 0.49 at τ = 0.155 — the turnover budget is load-bearing because a β-hedged book has lower vol than the 819 directional book (~61%/yr from ×15.48 over 4.6 yr at SR 0.97), so the same 11.9%/yr fee bill costs ~2.5× more Sharpe. BREAK-EVEN HOLDING: a position with edge m·σ̄ = 0.02·0.04 = 8 bp/day must be held ≥ 2c/(mσ̄) = 0.0042/0.0008 ≈ 5.3 days in expectation to pay its round trip ⇒ the forecast must have IC autocorrelation τ_IC ≥ ~5 days (regime-like features: 30 d VR, YZ vol) or GP cannot monetise it; this is pre-registered as gate K1''. MULTIPLICITY: SR0(N) = E[max_N SR|H0] ≈ σ_SR·E[max of N standard normals], σ_SR ≈ 1/√T_years; E[max Z_N] = 1.27/1.63/1.95 for N = 6/12/24. On 2024-01→2026-06 (T=2.5, σ_SR=0.63): SR0 = 0.80/1.03/1.23 — a bar of 0.97 is inside the null at N ≥ 12. On 2022-01→2026-06 (T=4.5, σ_SR=0.47): SR0 = 0.60/0.77/0.92. MinBTL ≈ (E[max Z_N]/SR*)²: N=6, SR*=0.97 → 1.7 yr; N=12 → 2.8 yr. Hence N ≤ 6 configurations (2 estimators × 3 controller settings), grade on the 4.5-yr OOS span with by-year positivity, and print SR0(N) beside every best cell.
profit_source: Forecast — of the tactic-conditional expected market-residual return E[p_{i,k,t}·e_{i,t+1} | x_{i,t}] per unit of the asset's own vol, which for the sign tactics (trend-L, reversal) is the CONDITIONAL LAG-L AUTOCORRELATION REGIME of residual returns, ≈ 0.80·ρ_L(x) in σ-units, ∝ σ²(VR_L(x) − 1) (Dao et al. 2016). It is a first-moment quantity in the sign-augmented information set — the loops-panel identity is not escaped — but it is a different quantity from TASK_915's unconditional E[e|x]: it can be nonzero in dispersion while zero in mean. Explicitly NOT claimed: risk premium (the book is β-hedged; a dollar-volume/size loading would be a risk premium and is a named attribution risk), rebalancing premium (constant-mix is a control arm only — measured negative on PIT, `POWERED_RESULT.md` B&H row via `backtest.py:225-227`, and second-order under arithmetic Sharpe), cost reduction (the turnover budget only keeps the cost drag at ≈0.19 rather than 0.49 Sharpe; it creates nothing).
why_learning: Four things a closed-form estimator cannot use as efficiently: (1) INTERACTION — the truth is E[e|x] = s(x_trend)·g(x_regime); a linear forecaster of e sees E_s[s·g] ≈ 0; the tactic-PnL target absorbs the known sign and makes g(x) a main effect, and a GBM then models the threshold/regime shape of g in the range-ratio, VR and vol-trend features without a hand-chosen cutoff (the 813 lesson: hand cutoffs on n=6 events are selection luck). (2) PARAMETER SHARING — one model over 273 assets × 8 tactics × ~1640 OOS days; the per-asset closed-form alternative (trailing mean of each asset's tactic PnL, i.e. factor/strategy momentum, Ehsani–Linnainmaa) estimates 273×8 means from ~60–120 noisy days each (SE ≈ 1/√90 ≈ 0.10 σ-units against a signal of 0.02); pooling with asset-invariant features borrows strength across the cross-section, and trend/reversal arms share one g(x) (mirror targets), halving the effective noise. (3) EVENT-CONDITIONAL STRUCTURE — dispersion, range and volume shocks (gap 4 in the record) enter as features; the model decides whether they modulate g(x) rather than a pre-registered rule guessing which of the 132 trigger cells matters. (4) NONLINEARITY OF COST-AWARE SIZING — the net target already contains the tactic's own turnover cost, so the fitted E[y|x] is directly comparable to the entry threshold 2cθ/σ̂; a closed-form ρ̂ estimate would have to be converted through an assumed scale. The discipline that keeps this honest: the strategy-momentum estimator IS the pre-registered baseline B0 and a feature; if the learner does not beat it by ≥ 0.005 IC, learning is declared dead and the closed-form selector is what remains.

bear_positive.argument: Positive in expectation in ANY bear iff gate K1 passes, because the book is market-residual by construction (β-hedged aim, Σ aim_i β̂_i = 0) so its sign in 2022 is not the market's sign; and the tactic library contains both directions on every asset, with the short leg legal on Kraken spot margin (borrow cost unmodelled — an open doubt). It is NOT guaranteed on the specific BEAR22 window: (a) BEAR22 is OUT of sample for the learner here (first refit trains on 2019–2021 with 13–84 live names, `POWERED_RESULT.md` coverage), so it is a real but low-power test; (b) the record's only bear-positive behaviour so far is the trend short leg (898: BEAR22 baseline +1.095 vs long-flat −2.471), which is one of the eight arms, so a learner that merely re-discovers 'trend-30 short in 2022' passes the form check without proving anything new; (c) if the learner's edge in 2022 came through a dollar-volume/size loading it would be a risk premium with liquidity-crash beta, hence the by-feature-group attribution is pre-registered. Pre-registered FAIL: BEAR22 net@21 ≤ 0 with CI hi < +0.5, or flat share in 2022 > 50%.

guards: 887 ADAPTIVE HOLD COLLAPSE: flat is an explicit arm with known PnL 0; the controller goes flat only where every asset's |f|·σ̂/θ < 2c, and that event is logged per day; pre-registered FAIL if flat days > 50% on 2024-01→2026-06 or median daily gross < 0.5 (`pathway.md:15` 'holds positions'); the strategy-momentum baseline B0 is blended at a FIXED a-priori weight (0.5) into f so the book never depends on the learner alone and collapse of the learner reverts to a known rule, not to HOLD. 892 RE-TRIM DAMAGE: trades happen only through the partial-adjustment law with a no-trade band (θ, δ frozen on train), turnover budget ≤ 0.06/day (vs 819's 0.155; 892 found the anti-edge lived in maintenance re-trims Δ −0.050..−0.062, entries/exits null); pre-registered decomposition of PnL into entry/exit legs vs re-trim legs against a frozen-hold counterfactual, re-trim leg must be ≥ 0 or the band widens on a pre-declared schedule (δ → 2δ), never by search; the 830 hold-shares vs constant-dollar effect (BEAR22 gross +0.225 vs +1.218, `experiments/830_corridor/SPEC.md:95-98`) is handled by charging drift re-trims explicitly (tactics panel corr. 3). 813 SELECTION LUCK: zero per-asset fitting (one pooled model); K=8 fixed before the first fit, feature list frozen in the SPEC with sha256; the grid graded on OOS is N ≤ 6 configurations (2 estimators × 3 controller settings); SR0(N) = E[max SR_N|H0] printed beside every best cell (0.60/0.77/0.92 for N = 6/12/24 on the 4.5-yr span; 0.80/1.03/1.23 on 2.5 yr), MinBTL stated (1.7 yr at N=6); Bonferroni over 18 IC cells (9 targets × 2 estimators); two dependence-preserving placebos (circular shift ≥ 60 d per asset; block-Rademacher sign flips of e) replace 819 CAPACITY's four-draw floor; by-year positivity in 2024, 2025, 2026H1 separately; ≥ 3 GBM seeds each reported. INSTRUMENT: unmodified `trader.backtest.cell_metrics` (seed 819, n_boot 2000, tiers 8/21) with simple-return series reported alongside the log-return default (`backtest.py:221-223`), and the 882 two-instrument discipline (eval_vector with quantised weights) only if K2 is reached.

why_not_falsified.receipt: `experiments/LEDGER.md` row 898/trend-decay: baseline net@8 2024 +0.041 → 2025 +0.663 → 2026H1 −1.659, no recent CI excluding 0; `fable_tactics_panel_2026-09-04.md:60-64` — 'the persistence diagnostic ... has never been run here'; `experiments/901_range_based_dependence_probe/range_probe.py` docstring — VR there is a bootstrap block-length tool
why_not_falsified.argument: 898 measured ONE tactic (30 d sign trend, equal weight, H=1) UNCONDITIONALLY on the whole panel. A mean of ≈0 is compatible with a nonzero dispersion of conditional autocorrelation across (asset, day). Whether OHLC state predicts the SIGN and MAGNITUDE of a tactic's next-period PnL — the quantity this mechanism learns — has never been measured on this panel at any horizon.

why_not_falsified.receipt: `docs/findings/modeling_surface_exhausted.md:57-66`: 813 = 132 pre-registered cells at minute scale, GO on n=6 BTC-spike episodes, hold-out n=25 inverted to net −4.08 / gross −3.27, precision 0.28
why_not_falsified.argument: 813 tested per-asset DISCRETE triggers with hand cutoffs on 6–28 events and best-of-132 selection. Here: one pooled model over ~350k asset-days × 8 tactics, no per-asset parameters, K and features frozen a priori, N ≤ 6 graded configurations with SR0(N) printed. The failure mode 813 exhibited is the one this design is built not to have; its result is about selection procedure, not about daily tactic-PnL predictability.

The range-ratio, Yang–Zhang, vol-of-vol, dollar-volume and dispersion features this mechanism uses have never been inputs to any daily object in the repo; the loops panel's own reading (pt 6) is that 887 measured a learning/search failure, not absent edge.

It bounds nothing about this target.

why_not_falsified.receipt: `fable_self_learning_loops_panel_2026-09-05.md` — identity E[gross] = Σ E[w_t·E[r_{t+1}|F_t]]; continual-learning row: 'only Var_t(IC_t)·φ ... read with less variance by a by-year IC'
why_not_falsified.argument: The loops panel refutes loops that create no conditional mean; this mechanism claims none — it forecasts E[s·e|x], a conditional mean in an enlarged information set. The panel's own surviving item (time-variation of the conditional mean is the harvestable quantity) is exactly the dispersion this design targets, estimated by a pooled supervised regression rather than by re-fitting a policy — the estimator the panel said is the efficient one.

literature.ref: Dao, Nguyen, Deremble, Lempérière, Bouchaud, Potters 2016, 'Tail protection for long investors: Trend convexity at work', arXiv:1607.02410
literature.claim: Trend-following performance equals the difference between long-term and short-term realised variance for many trend definitions, i.e. E[PnL_trend,L] ∝ σ²(VR_L − 1); the sign flips for reversal. This is the identity that makes tactic PnL a second-moment/autocorrelation functional.
literature.numbers: Decomposition G_T = (λ/2)(S_T−S_0)² − (λ/2)ΣD_t² (as quoted in the tactics panel); no Sharpe numbers in the abstract.

literature.ref: Lempérière, Deremble, Seager, Potters, Bouchaud 2014, 'Two centuries of trend following', arXiv:1404.3274
literature.claim: Trend excess returns are statistically robust over two centuries but 'shorter trends have significantly withered' while long trends show no degradation — a prior that the dispersion this mechanism hunts is likelier at L=30–90 than L=1–10.
literature.numbers: t-stat ≈ 5 since 1960, ≈ 10 since 1800; saturation for large signals.

literature.ref: Ehsani & Linnainmaa 2022 JF, 'Factor momentum and the momentum factor' (NBER w25551)
literature.claim: Strategy (factor) returns are positively autocorrelated, so the trailing mean of a strategy's own PnL predicts its next return — the closed-form baseline B0 this learner must beat and the reason B0 is also a feature.
literature.numbers: Average factor earns 1 bp/month after a losing year vs 53 bp/month after a positive year.

literature.ref: Moreira & Muir 2017 JF, 'Volatility-managed portfolios' (NBER w22208); Cederburg, O'Doherty, Wang, Yan 2020 JFE (via `fable_tactics_panel_2026-09-04.md:70-72`)
literature.claim: Scaling by inverse trailing variance raises factor Sharpe in-sample; Cederburg et al. find the gain significant for only 8/103 strategies, momentum being the exception — supports keeping the vol-targeted trend arm k7 as one tactic while not claiming sizing as an edge source.
literature.numbers: Cederburg: 8/103 significant; MOM Sharpe 0.48 → 0.99. Moreira–Muir page fetched gives no numbers.

literature.ref: López de Prado 2018, Advances in Financial Machine Learning, ch. 3 §3.6 'Meta-labeling' (Hudson & Thames exposition fetched)
literature.claim: Primary model supplies the side, a secondary model predicts whether that bet is profitable and its probability sets the size; improves F1 by removing false positives at high recall. This is the structural template for the classifier arm; the regression-on-net-tactic-PnL arm is its magnitude-aware variant.
literature.numbers: No Sharpe/precision numbers in the fetched exposition (MNIST toy example only).

literature.ref: Bailey, Borwein, López de Prado, Zhu 2014, 'Pseudo-mathematics and financial charlatanism', Notices AMS 61(5) (fetch returned 403; prior knowledge)
literature.claim: Expected maximum in-sample Sharpe under the null over N trials and the minimum backtest length: SR0(N) ≈ σ_SR[(1−γ)Φ⁻¹(1−1/N) + γΦ⁻¹(1−1/(Ne))], MinBTL ≈ (E[max Z_N]/SR*)²; the basis of the SR0(N) guard.
literature.numbers: E[max Z_N] ≈ 1.27/1.63/1.95 for N=6/12/24; with σ_SR = 1/√T: SR0(6) = 0.80 on 2.5 yr, 0.60 on 4.5 yr; MinBTL 1.7 yr for N=6 at SR* 0.97.

literature.ref: Bariviera 2017 'The inefficiency of Bitcoin revisited'; Takaishi & Adachi 2019 'Market efficiency, liquidity, and multifractality of Bitcoin'; Takaishi 2021; Tang et al. 2024 'Stylized facts of high-frequency Bitcoin time series' (arXiv API summaries)
literature.claim: Bitcoin's Hurst exponent is time-varying and has drifted toward 0.5 (efficiency) since 2013–14; regime shifts in H are identifiable ex post. Consistent with 898's decay of the unconditional trend mean; none of these abstracts quantifies the PERSISTENCE of local H regimes, which is exactly the unmeasured quantity gate K1'' tests.

literature.ref: Liu, Tsyvinski, Wu 2022 JF, 'Common risk factors in cryptocurrency' (NBER w25882)
literature.claim: Market, size and momentum factors price the crypto cross-section — cross-sectional momentum existed historically (arm k6), and a dollar-volume feature can load on the SIZE premium, which would be a risk premium, hence the by-feature-group attribution guard.
literature.numbers: Three-factor result; horizons and Sharpe not in the fetched abstract.

literature.ref: Parkinson 1980 JBus; Garman & Klass 1980 JBus; Yang & Zhang 2000 JBus; Lo & MacKinlay 1988 RFS (prior knowledge; YZ also cited at `fable_direction_memo_2026-09-03.md:132-134`)
literature.claim: Range-based variance estimators are 5–14× more efficient than close-to-close (Parkinson ≈ 5.2, GK ≈ 7.4, YZ up to ≈ 14, drift-independent with opening jumps); the Parkinson/close-to-close ratio therefore estimates sub-daily autocorrelation (a variance-ratio statistic) with ≈ √5 smaller SE than a close-based Lo–MacKinlay VR(q) of the same window — the OHLC-native content of the feature set.
literature.numbers: Efficiency 5.2 / 7.4 / ≤14; SE of a 30-bar ratio ≈ 0.12 vs ≈ 0.26 close-based.

literature.ref: Gârleanu & Pedersen 2013 JF, 'Dynamic trading with predictable returns and transaction costs' (second-hand via `fable_direction_memo_2026-09-03.md:287-295`)
literature.claim: With quadratic costs the optimal book is partial adjustment toward an aim portfolio that weights slower-decaying signals more: x_t = x_{t−1} + Λ⁻¹A(aim_t − x_{t−1}); the control law here is its one-parameter (θ) form plus a Davis–Norman-style no-trade band for the proportional 21 bp cost.
literature.numbers: Trade rate θ ∈ {0.25, 0.5}; implied mean holding 1/θ = 2–4 days plus band; break-even holding ≥ 5.3 days at m = 0.02, σ̄ = 4%.

controllability: High, by construction — this is the operator's 'better hold on policy' requirement met literally. The action grammar is K=8 pre-registered deterministic rules plus flat; every daily decision is 'asset i: forecast f (σ-units) from tactic mix {μ̂_k}, aim a, traded Δx = θ(a − x) or 0 (in band)', logged and reproducible from the OHLCV panel and one GBM file (a few MB). Turnover is bounded by θ and δ (frozen; ≤ 0.06/day expected), gross by Σ|aim| ≤ 1 and w_max = 5%, market exposure by the β-hedge; there is no self-play, no search, no learned policy checkpoint, no in-loop refit (quarterly refits with a frozen recipe and a sha256'd feature list). Drift monitoring is built in: trailing 90-day realised per-date IC of f against e/σ̂ is compared monthly to the pre-registered placebo band; if it falls below the placebo median for two consecutive months the book reverts to the fixed B0 blend or to flat and the event is recorded — the 887 attractor becomes a logged, reversible state, not a silent collapse. Failure attribution is separable: gate K1 (signal), K1' (learning vs closed-form), K1'' (persistence), K2 (controller/cost) each name a different culprit, so a FAIL says which half failed — the property the MuZero line lacked (memo §0.2). Existing surfaces are reused unmodified: `trader/data.py` aggregation, the 819 POWERED PIT builder, `trader.backtest.cell_metrics`, `RiskConfig` caps; the new code is one OHLCV panel builder, eight rule functions, a feature module, a LightGBM fit/predict wrapper and the controller — small enough for a ≤1-page SPEC per `pathway.md:91-94`.
compute: CPU only. Panel: `ohlcv_daily` already exists and is what 898 read (ends 2026-07-06; TASK_899 backfill closes the 2026H1 seam) — minutes to load 273 assets × ~2800 days × 6 fields; tactic matrices and features: numpy, seconds to minutes. Learning: ~2.8M rows × ~30 features; LightGBM with ≤300 trees, depth ≤ 6 fits in ~1–3 min on 8 cores; 18 quarterly refits × 2 estimators × 3 seeds ≈ 108 fits ≈ 2–5 CPU-hours; ridge control is closed form. Scoring: `cell_metrics` with n_boot 2000 per cell × ≤ 6 configs × regimes: minutes. Placebos (200 circular-shift draws for the IC null) add ≤ 2 CPU-hours if run at reduced tree count. Total ≤ 1 CPU-day, RAM < 8 GB, safe_run-wrapped on gpu-server CPU (or the workstation under the caps in `.claude/rules/10-compute-allocation.md`). GPU requirement: none. The 64 GB cards are irrelevant to every stage; the only conceivable GPU use is an optional shared-MLP third arm (minutes on one 24 GB card), which is out of the pre-registered grid.

kill_experiment.design: Three stages, all pre-registered in a ≤1-page SPEC (sha256 recorded before the first fit), CPU only. STAGE 0 (hours): build the PIT OHLCV daily panel; emit the K=8 tactic position matrices; score each tactic alone by year and regime at net@0/8/21 through `cell_metrics` (this doubles as the tactics panel's row-1 hull: best fixed mixture, ex-post oracle selector, random-selector null over 200 seeds — if the oracle selector's net@21 on 2024-01→2026-06 is < +0.97, stop: no selector over this library can clear the bar). STAGE 1 (the load-bearing measurement, ≤ 1 CPU-day): expanding-window quarterly refits from 2019-01, 21-day embargo, OOS 2022-01→2026-06, estimators ridge and LightGBM-Huber (3 seeds), targets y_{i,k} for k=1..8 and the pooled asset-level f; statistics per estimator×target: per-date cross-sectional Spearman IC (mean by year, Newey–West t with lag 1), the IC autocorrelation τ_IC (persistence), the strategy-momentum baseline B0 IC (trailing 90 d mean of y_{i,k}), and the pooled-unconditional baseline B1 (best tactic by trailing global mean). Placebos: circular shift of targets by ≥ 60 days per asset (dependence-preserving) and block-Rademacher sign flips of e (kills the conditional mean, keeps |e|, σ, ranges) — 200 draws each → null IC distribution. Also measure N_eff = (Σλ)²/Σλ² of the residual correlation spectrum by year (closes TASK_825's parked measurement as a by-product). STAGE 2 (only on K1 pass, hours): the book — f → aim → partial adjustment with (θ, δ) ∈ 3 pre-declared settings, β-hedged, PIT, 2022-01→2026-06; `cell_metrics` net@8/21 by regime with block-bootstrap CI; flat share, median gross, turnover, entry/exit vs re-trim PnL decomposition against a frozen-hold counterfactual; by-feature-group attribution (range / VR / flow / xs / tactic-state) via leave-group-out refits on the winning cell; SR0(N) for N = 6 printed beside the result. Kill date: 14 days from SPEC commit; the grid is fixed, additions are new rows.
kill_experiment.instrument: `trader/data.py::aggregate_asset_daily` (OHLCV, `trader/data.py:150-190`) via a sibling OHLCV panel builder (the existing `build_daily_panel_from_db` drops O/H/L/V, `:190-227`); PIT universe from the 819 POWERED builder (273 assets, dead coins retained); unmodified `trader.backtest.cell_metrics` (seed 819, n_boot 2000, gate tiers 8/21, one-sided cost on Σ|Δpos|, `trader/backtest.py:188-227`) with the simple-return series reported alongside the log-return default (`backtest.py:221-223`); LightGBM + scikit-learn ridge; Newey–West SE; SR0(N) per Bailey–López de Prado; epoch named post-E-d with the 899 seam pinned per `LEDGER.md:28-41`. If K2 is reached, the 882 two-instrument discipline (eval_vector `--operator policy-argmax --vector-weight-rebalance` with weights quantised to the ±w_unit ladder) must agree within 0.1.
kill_experiment.pass_fail: K1 SIGNAL: for the pooled asset-level f or any single tactic target, mean per-date IC ≥ 0.02 on 2024-01→2026-06, NW t ≥ 3 after Bonferroni over 18 cells (9 targets × 2 estimators), IC > 0 in each of 2024, 2025, 2026H1 separately, and observed IC > the 95th percentile of both placebo nulls. K1' LEARNING: the winning estimator's IC exceeds the strategy-momentum baseline B0 by ≥ 0.005 with the paired NW t ≥ 2; otherwise learning is DEAD here and the closed-form selector is what survives (still routed to K2 as a non-learned book). K1'' PERSISTENCE: τ_IC (first lag where the IC autocorrelation drops below 1/e) ≥ 5 days, the break-even holding at m = 0.02 — a signal that passes K1 but fails K1'' is real and unmonetisable at 21 bp and is recorded as such. K2 CONTROL: net@21 ≥ +0.97 on 2024-01→2026-06 with bootstrap CI lo > 0 AND above SR0(N=6) = 0.80 on that span (or ≥ +0.97 on 2022-01→2026-06 where SR0(6) = 0.60), all 3 GBM seeds ≥ +0.56, positive in each of 2024/2025/2026H1 and on BEAR22 (OOS for the learner), flat days ≤ 50%, median gross ≥ 0.5, turnover ≤ 0.06/day, re-trim leg PnL ≥ 0 vs frozen-hold; MARGINAL if ≥ +0.56 with CI straddling 0. FAIL CONSEQUENCES, pre-committed: K1 fails everywhere → tactic-PnL on daily OHLC is unpredictable from state; no selector over deterministic daily tactics (Hedge, ridge, MuZero over K arms) can clear the bar; the sign-conditional cell is added to TASK_915's verdict and the tactics lane closes. K1 passes / K1' fails → ship nothing learned; the factor-momentum selector goes to K2 as a rule. K1 passes / K2 fails → controller or cost is the culprit, the memo's first legitimate re-entry point for a search-based controller with the forecast already measured. Stage-0 oracle-selector < +0.97 → stop before any fit.
kill_experiment.cost: ≤ 1 CPU-day of compute (safe_run-wrapped; no GPU); ~2–3 engineer-days for the OHLCV builder, eight rules, features, fit wrapper, controller and SPEC; zero server GPU time; no deploy. Kill date 14 days from SPEC commit.

honest_odds: P(K1: pooled tactic-PnL per-date IC ≥ 0.02 sustained on 2024–26H1, placebo-clean) ≈ 15–20%. P(K1' | K1: learner beats the closed-form strategy-momentum baseline by ≥ 0.005 IC) ≈ 50%. P(K1'' | K1: persistence ≥ 5 days) ≈ 60%. P(K2 | K1∧K1'': net@21 ≥ +0.97 PIT with CI lo > 0, 3 seeds, bear-positive, holds positions) ≈ 35%. Unconditional P(goalposts) ≈ 5–7%; P(≥ +0.56 MARGINAL) ≈ 10–12%. Slightly above the tactics panel's 3–5% because the target transformation and cross-asset pooling are a real efficiency gain and four of the eight arms are unmeasured, but not much above it: the quantity is still a conditional mean, 898 says the dominant autocorrelation regime has averaged ≈ 0 since 2024, the Hurst literature says Bitcoin has drifted to H ≈ 0.5, and the mechanism needs DISPERSION of |VR(30)−1| ≥ 0.10–0.16 around that zero with a predictable sign and ≥ 5-day persistence. The FAIL branch is worth the CPU-day: it retires every selector over daily deterministic tactics at once.
open_doubts: N_eff of the β-hedged residual panel is unmeasured (TASK_825 parked); the 819 directional book calibrates to N_eff ≈ 1.4. If the residual panel's N_eff is 3–5 rather than 10–20, the required m rises to ≈ 0.035–0.045 (ρ_30 ≈ 0.045–0.055, |VR(30)−1| ≈ 0.25), a regime the record suggests is rare after 2023.

Overlap with TASK_915: a GBM on F1+F2 there can in principle learn s(x_trend)·g(x_regime) from the raw target; this design's incremental value is representational (main effect vs interaction) and in the B0 comparison and deployable form. If 915 G-A fails on every cell including GBM with trend+range features, the K1 prior here should be revised down (not to zero — the targets differ).

The break-even holding (≥ 5.3 days at m = 0.02, σ̄ = 4%) may exceed the lifetime of the autocorrelation regimes the features detect; K1'' tests it, but a PASS on K1 with FAIL on K1'' is the most likely non-null outcome and yields no book.

Borrow cost and availability on the Kraken spot-margin short leg are unmodelled; a β-hedged book is ~50% short by construction, so a 5–15%/yr borrow rate on shorts would cost 0.1–0.3 Sharpe on a 25–30%-vol residual book.

Residual construction on a changing PIT universe: β̂ from a 90-day window on new listings is noisy and the equal-weight market itself changes composition; a misestimated β leaks market direction into e and would make the 'residual' book partly directional — check Σ x_i β̂_i realised exposure ex post.
Yang–Zhang σ̂ on illiquid names with zero-range days needs a floor (VOL_FLOOR exists); without it standardised targets explode and Huber saturates — a construction risk, not a signal question.

The 21 bp tier is asserted, not observed (Kraken's ladder has no 16 bp tier; operator tier unrecorded — loops panel pt 1); ±5 bp moves the cost term by ±0.001 in m and ±0.05 in Sharpe at τ = 0.06 — second-order, but the record should write the tier down before any book is graded.

A dollar-volume/size loading could pass K1 as a risk premium (Liu–Tsyvinski–Wu size factor) rather than a forecast; the by-feature-group attribution is pre-registered but a mixed source would blur the profit-source accounting.

Stage-0 hull: if the ex-post oracle selector over the eight arms is below +0.97 on 2024–26 (the tactics panel's STEP-0), the whole design stops before a single fit — a real possibility given constant-mix and trend are both ≈ 0 or negative there; the reversal and vol-targeted arms are the unknowns that decide it.

Only two literature items were read at abstract level with numbers this session (Dao 2016, Ehsani–Linnainmaa); Bailey–López de Prado and the range-estimator efficiencies are from prior knowledge (search-snippet depth) and should be re-verified before the SPEC quotes them.
